page.overview:
What is Charlie's Project?

Charlie's Project is an experimental robot created by Charlotte Emily for her robotics class in college. Consisting of two faces on a length board, her goal was to teach robots natural spoken language by having them listen to people talking around them and to them. While Charlie never managed to get them working properly, components of her experiment would later be used by her friends to sneak past hostile animatronics.

Charlie's project is two mechanical faces held upright on metal structures and attached to a length board. The identical faces are smooth, nearly featureless and made of malleable plastic. They are said to look like unfinished statues, with blind eyes that are only raised bumps in the molded plastic. The faces also have lips that move but never part. At the back of their heads are networks of casing, microchips, and wires. The length board the heads are wired to is a large, black box with knobs and buttons. Charlie’s experiment needs to be plugged in with a cord, and a small black switch activates it. Upon activation, an array of red and green little lights blink and tiny cooling fans start.

While in college at St. George, Charlie works on a project to teach natural spoken language to computers and programming. Using spare parts from her father's house, including Theodore, she creates two plastic faces held upright on metal structures and attached to a length board. There are two components to her project, the first being switches that make them move and talk only to each other. The other component is a repurposed hearing aid that allows the faces to listen to everything around them. This is always on, however they only collect the data and not interact with it. When Charlie isn’t working on them, she covers her experiment with a pillowcase.

One day, Charlie arrives at the dorm a little under an hour before her date with John and decides to work on her project more. Upon activating them, the two faces look at each other with constrained movements and speak a total of six words before stopping. Charlie turns them off and begins adjusting wires until she hears Jessica arriving and quickly covers them with the pillowcase. Jessica convinces her to show off the project, but when she becomes concerned Charlie quickly turns it off again and lovingly replaces the pillowcase. She then explains that she isn't exactly programming the faces to do anything, rather she's helping them learn on their own. When Charlie returns to the dorm to get ready for her date, she glances at the faces under the pillowcase and worries that, like Jessica, John wouldn't understand it if she showed him.
